A knowledge base is only as useful as the material that reaches it, and the material rarely arrives in one shape. Notes live in text files, reports arrive as PDFs, and the person who wrote the specification probably used Word. A compiler that accepts a single extension quietly narrows the corpus it was built to reason over, and the narrowing is invisible until a question is asked about a document that never made it in. The fixtures in this directory exist to keep that failure observable: each one holds a sentence whose exact wording the suite asserts on, so extraction can be checked without depending on a parser's formatting choices. They are deliberately small, generated by this script, and safe to regenerate at any time without touching the assertions that read them.
